overview: This table controls the downloadable content banners in the main menu, including their titles, pictures, and which appear first.
description: Defines the main-menu DLC store banners: localized DLC-name text keys, full and small resolution-dependent texture IDs, and the save-progress bit that marks a DLC acquired and controls carousel ordering.

Id.simple: The name the game uses to find this banner in its main-menu banner list.
Id.technical: FName declared as FGameDataTableRow_Banner::Id and named as the DataTable ImportKeyField; the export spells the stored value ID. RefreshBanners collects rows with FGameDataTableArray::GetRows in table/row-name order, skips UserProgressFlag == -1, partitions the surviving Row->Id values by the current flag bit, appends unacquired IDs before acquired ones, and passes BannerIds[0] to SetBanner when the resulting list is non-empty. SetBanner calls UDataTable::FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_Banner>(BannerId, TEXT(""), false) on each BannerDataTables entry and stops at the first hit; a miss returns before changing CurrentBannerId, the acquired/new icons, caption, pagination, or textures, and emits no warning. The ID is otherwise used only as the row key and as the value carried through BannerIds / SlideBanner.

Id_BannerMessage.simple: The translated title shown on the banner, such as the name of a downloadable story or outfit pack.
Id_BannerMessage.technical: FName passed unchanged to BannerText->SetTextIdOnly when SetBanner selects the row. SetTextIdOnly creates a parameterless FGameTextRequest; GameTextManager routes only SYS_-prefixed IDs to SystemTextDataTable and resolves GLS_NAME_DLC_* from the current-language TextDataTables, whose first table is GlossaryTextDataTable_<language>. The export uses GLS_NAME_DLC_0110, GLS_NAME_DLC_0120, GLS_NAME_DLC_0210 and GLS_NAME_DLC_0220; the English glossary resolves them to Hidden Inventory/Premature Death, Anime Season 1 Ending Theme 1 Outfits, The Shibuya Incident and Kyoto Jujutsu High School Girls' Outfits respectively. These are localization keys, not literal display strings. The same keys appear in GameDlcContentDisplayNames for DLC07, DLC10, DLC08 and DLC11, matching the rows' progress flags.

BannerTextureName.simple: The name of the full-size banner picture. The game uses it on very high-resolution screens.
BannerTextureName.technical: FName used as a WidgetTexture primary-asset ID. MainMenuTop state 0 collects this field and SmallBannerTextureName from every collected banner row, creates WidgetTexture loaders, waits for them in state 1, then inserts each loaded UTexture2D into GameWidgetManager::DynamicLoadTextureMap under its FName key. SetBanner resolves both names with FindDynamicLoadTexture (null on a miss) and passes them to BannerButton->SetBannerTextures. The variable named LargeTexture is selected when the current screen-resolution X is at least HighResolutionThreshold (3840); below that threshold the small variant is selected instead, so the two fields are resolution alternatives rather than two simultaneously displayed images.

SmallBannerTextureName.simple: The name of the smaller banner picture. The game uses it on screens that are not very high resolution.
SmallBannerTextureName.technical: FName resolved through the same WidgetTexture-loader and GameWidgetManager::DynamicLoadTextureMap chain as BannerTextureName. SetBanner supplies it as SmallTexture to BannerButton->SetBannerTextures, which selects it when the current screen-resolution X is below HighResolutionThreshold (3840); at or above 3840 the large texture is used. MainMenuTop prefetches this name for every exported banner row, including any row with UserProgressFlag -1 that RefreshBanners excludes from the carousel.

UserProgressFlag.simple: Which downloadable content the banner checks for ownership. Owned banners show an acquired mark, and unowned banners appear first.
UserProgressFlag.technical: int32 bit index, defaulted to 0 by the reconstructed row constructor; exported values are 6, 7, 9 and 10. IsProgressFlagSet computes word = uint32(Flag) >> 2 and bit = uint32(Flag) & 3, rejects word >= 128 (the 128-word progress array), and otherwise tests GameManager::UserInfo.UserProgressFlagWords[word]. SetBanner uses the result only to swap NewIcon and AcquiredIcon visibility. RefreshBanners skips the exact -1 sentinel, partitions all other rows by the same bit, and puts unset flags before set ones; other negative values cast to a huge unsigned word and read as unset. Each exported flag is an entitlement bit set/cleared by GM_DiffDlcEntitlements from Steam receipts: 6 = DLC07 (BANNER_0110), 7 = DLC08 (BANNER_0210), 9 = DLC10 (BANNER_0120), 10 = DLC11 (BANNER_0220). Those DLC IDs have the same GLS text keys used by the rows' Id_BannerMessage fields. The DataTable manager loads the table into BannerDataTables only after all primary-asset DataTable loads complete.

notes: The sole export contains one BannerDataTable asset with four rows: BANNER_0110/flag 6/DLC07, BANNER_0120/flag 9/DLC10, BANNER_0220/flag 10/DLC11 and BANNER_0210/flag 7/DLC08. Their textures are T_UI_Banner_BannerImage_00..03 and T_UI_Banner_BannerImage_Small_00..03 in that row order. No localized or platform BannerDataTable variant was present among the supplied exports.

There is no display-order field. the main-menu OpenFriendIcon path calls RefreshBanners before opening the banner window, preserving the row collector's order within the unacquired and acquired partitions; arrows and the auto-slide tick then cycle BannerIds with wraparound. Pagination icons are initially created for every collected row, but SetBanner hides icons beyond the filtered BannerIds count.

These are DLC store promotions, not generic news entries: activating the banner opens SYS_DIALOG_MESSAGE_0501 (English: 'Proceed to the Steam Store?'), the Yes result sets main-menu selection 8 (Store), and the main-menu phase calls ShowDlcStore.

BannerDataTables is a TArray and both the row collector and SetBanner walk it with first-hit precedence, so duplicate row names across hypothetical extra tables would shadow later rows. StartInitialLoading registers only one loader named BannerDataTable and the available export has one asset, so banner sharding is a generic container capability, not observed retail data.

The export writes the row key property as ID while the header and ImportKeyField call it Id; they are the same native FName field. The reconstructed row constructor explicitly defaults only UserProgressFlag to 0; FName members default to NAME_None, and every exported row supplies all five values.

A missing BannerId is a silent SetBanner no-op (FindRow is called with warnings disabled). FindDynamicLoadTexture returns null for a missing texture name; no explicit null check occurs before the textures are passed to the banner button.

Behavior above is traced through reconstructed C++ annotated with retail addresses and the supplied DataTable/glossary exports. The retail banner UMG widget tree, bound widget names, actual texture packages and runtime screenshots were not available, so their asset-side wiring is not independently observed; the reconstruction guide states that gameplay logic is native C++ rather than Blueprint.

usages.detail: After all DataTable primary assets finish loading, resolves the BannerDataTable loader and adds the loaded UDataTable to BannerDataTables (+0xB60).
Collects every typed banner row across BannerDataTables; the count also drives one pagination icon per raw row at line 130.
SetBanner resolves BannerId by FindRow across all tables, then updates the flag icons, text key, pagination and the two dynamically cached textures.
RefreshBanners filters -1, partitions rows by current entitlement bit, places unacquired rows first, and selects BannerIds[0].
The banner tick decrements SlideRemainingTime and auto-advances with SlideBanner(true, false) when more than one banner is listed and auto-slide is enabled.
Main-menu preparation collects both texture FNames from every banner row and creates WidgetTexture loaders; lines 190-194 later place the loaded textures in the dynamic texture cache.
Chooses the supplied small or large texture by current width versus the 3840-pixel threshold and slides/promotes it into the centre banner image.
Main-menu startup calls RefreshBanners immediately before opening the banner window; input handling at line 492 advances it with NextMenu/PrevMenu.
Banner activation opens the Yes/No Steam-store confirmation; main-menu line 595 turns the Yes result into selected menu 8, which MainMenuTop line 457 handles with ShowDlcStore.
Routes non-SYS_ banner text IDs such as GLS_NAME_DLC_* to the language text tables, beginning with GlossaryTextDataTable_<language>.
Diffs Steam DLC receipts against the entitlement table and sets or clears the same UserProgressFlag bits that the banner rows reference.
